raw_user_query: How do plants make their food?

orchestrator_output.text_narration: Hello Praneeth! Today, we'll learn how plants, our green friends, prepare their own food. This amazing process is called Photosynthesis. Just like we need ingredients to cook, plants need sunlight, water from the soil, and carbon dioxide from the air. Chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves, helps capture sunlight. Inside the leaves, especially in tiny structures called stomata, water and carbon dioxide combine using sunlight's energy. This magical reaction creates glucose, which is the plant's food, and releases oxygen into the air. So, plants are autotrophs, meaning they make their own food. This process is vital for all life on Earth, as it provides food for animals and humans, and the oxygen we breathe!

steps.title: Absorption
steps.description: Plants absorb water through roots and CO2 through stomata. Chlorophyll captures sunlight.

steps.title: Conversion
steps.description: Sunlight energy converts water and CO2 into glucose (food) and oxygen.

steps.title: Output
steps.description: Glucose is used as food by the plant, and oxygen is released into the atmosphere.
